extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, patent examiners, and judges
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and legal standards for drafting the specification (description) and claims of a patent, covering machines, manufactures, compositions of matter, designs, and improvements; focuses on sufficiency, particularity, and what must be disclosed so skilled persons can practise the invention. Useful for practitioners preparing or evaluating US-style patent specifications and claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete description of manufacture (enumerate essential qualities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where its essential qualities are discernible these may be enumerated, and if this can be so clearly and precisely done as not only to give a complete knowledge of the new manufacture, but also to distinguish it from all others, it is the best mode of describing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the product can be understood and distinguished without describing the process, the product-description suffices; other assertions regarding it are immaterial. Examples/anti-patterns: enumerating essential qualities is preferred; merely asserting novelty without clear distinguishing qualities is defective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Known parts and common elements need not be described
rubrics_metrics.description: Parts of machinery and processes generally known need not be described; a wedge, pulleys, rollers, rack and pinion, and other things known to all mechanics will be supplied by the mechanist without stating their size or structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not waste specification space on elements of ordinary skill. However, when the relation of known parts to the invention affects its operation or distinction from the prior art, describe sufficiently to show the invention's limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustment-level details (sizes, velocities, proportions) not essential
rubrics_metrics.description: Utmost precision in the description of the machine is not to be expected, nor is it essential. Nor is it essential to state the proportionate parts of a machine, nor the velocity of its operations. These are matters of adjustment for the eye and judgment of the constructor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not require exact dimensions or operating speeds unless such parameters are essential to produce the invention's novel effect. If exactness is required, the specification must supply it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe by mode of production when product inseparable from process
rubrics_metrics.description: A manufacture may be described by describing its mode of production, if no better way exists; and a product may be described and claimed as the result of a described process when the manufacture is inseparably connected with the mode of production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the product cannot be identified independently of the process, limit the patent to the product when produced by that process. Example: chemical products sometimes must be described by the process that produces them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of matter: three essential descriptive subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: A composition of matter presents three essential subjects for description: the ingredients, their mode of intermixture, and the resulting composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each ingredient must be completely and exactly described (by common name or qualities); nothing must be left to experiment as to their nature or number; do not specify substances as ingredients unless essential. The composition itself can be described by enumerating essential qualities or as the result of the intermixture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantities and proportions must be stated precisely (or limits given)
rubrics_metrics.description: In describing the mode of intermixture, the quantity and proportions of the several ingredients, and the process of compounding them, must be correctly and precisely stated. Where quantities and proportions must be exact in order to produce the composition, the Description must furnish this exact rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If allowable variations exist, state definite limits that are consistent with attaining the desired result (e.g., ranges like 'from 1 lb. to 10 lb.'). The word 'about' will be disregarded and the quantity named taken as exact; vague statements that require experiment render the specification insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intermixture/process acts and means must be specified unless obvious
rubrics_metrics.description: The intermixture of ingredients is an art or process, and must be described in the same manner as any other art, each act with the physical means for performing it being specified unless already obvious to those skilled in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe each step and the tools/means when not obvious to a skilled practitioner. Use of customary technical terms for the narrow circle of persons familiar with the art is permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use customary technical terms appropriate to the art
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor may employ such technical terms as are customary in the art to which the composition belongs, however narrow may be the circle of persons familiar with that art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifications address persons skilled in the art; tailored technical language is acceptable, but ensure that such terms are those a skilled practitioner would understand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design descriptions must point out characteristic qualities and distinguish new from old
rubrics_metrics.description: So far as practicable, the written Description of a design must point out its characteristic qualities and accurately distinguish between what is claimed as new and what is conceded to be old. Taken in connection with the drawings, it must impart to the public a knowledge of the design and of the method of producing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide drawings and textual pointers to the novel visual features; do not include mechanical functions in a design description (if shape creates mechanical properties, treat them as a manufacture, not a design). If obverse and reverse differ, describe both.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvement specifications must describe both the improvement and original sufficiently
rubrics_metrics.description: An improvement must be described in all its essential characteristics like any other invention, and in addition the original invention, of whose idea this is a new development, must be delineated sufficiently to show the nature of the whole invention as improved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish clearly between old and new so the public can identify where the improvement begins. If the original is patented and available, a reference may suffice; if not, describe the original to the extent necessary to understand the improvement and how it is attached or combined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description must enable a person skilled in the art to practise the invention without further experiment
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must be in such full, clear, and exact terms as to enable any one skilled in the art to which it appertains to compound and use the invention; nothing must be left to experiment either as to the nature or number of ingredients or the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sufficiency is judged by whether skilled persons could reproduce the invention from the specification alone. If the description is so incomplete as to be useless for public information, the court may declare the patent void without witness testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of description is a question of fact for the jury (subject-matter experts)
rubrics_metrics.description: The sufficiency of the Description is a question of fact, to be investigated by experience, elucidated by evidence, and decided by a jury. Only persons skilled in the art are usually capable of judging whether delineations are correct, complete, and intelligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare factual evidence and expert testimony when asserting or defending sufficiency. Courts may nonetheless resolve pure legal constructions of claim language as questions of law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of patent: claims must particularly point out and distinctly claim the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the office of the Claim to define the limits of that exclusive use which is secured to the inventor by the patent. The statutes require that he shall particularly point out and distinctly claim the part, improvement, or combination which he claims as his invention or discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims must conclude the specification and be specific and distinct for every separate subject matter claimed. They define the public boundary between allowed and disclaimed subject matter; vague or absent claims render the application deficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product vs process coverage: if product cannot be recognized apart from process, patent may cover it only when made by that process
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless a product is so described that it can be recognised apart from the description of the process of making it, the patent will cover it only when made by that process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When drafting, either (a) describe the product so it is recognizable independently, or (b) limit the claim to the product produced by the specified process. If both product and machine/process are described, product description may suffice even if the machine is useless.
